doc.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Visual uses of the music and the film Journey of the Heart
summary: The Today Show segment, and returning to film with Karen Arthur's movie after 14 years.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: The music, a lot of it seems to lend itself to some visual images. Has anybody ever approached you about doing that?

The only thing, years and years and years and years ago there was piece done on The Today Show with a photographer. It was about a photographer. Boyd Matson, I was trying to think of his name, Boyd Matson was the moderator and Bob Flick had something to do with that before he joined as head writer for, he’s now retired, from Entertainment Tonight. So the segment was about a photographer and they used the Cello Quartet music and it worked beautifully. So my wife is in video and she’s thought about it for many years. We’ll get into it.
Great. You’ve done some fairly well known films, and do you like writing for film?

Yeah. I haven’t done it for a long time. I mean I left it for about 14 years until about a year and a half ago when this director called me, Karen Arthur called me and said I’ve got this project that you should really think about it. So it was called “Journey of the Heart,” it was about an autistic savant from Waltham, Massachusetts, unbelievably. That’s where he lives, where I went to junior high school, and starring Cybil Shepherd. So I did this movie for CBS and I really enjoy it. I enjoy it a lot. So I’m putting together some midi ideas and gear and thinking about getting more into technology.
